greek: Καὶ ἦν πᾶσα ἡ γῆ χεῖλος ἕν, καὶ φωνὴ μία πᾶσιν.
hint: All the earth had one lip and one sound.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ûdĕbārîm ʾăḥādîm*, *and the same words*. The Greek has *one sound*, φωνή, and adds *to all*.
*A lip*, the Hebrew *śāpâ*, which is *lip* and *language* both; Middle Liddell gives χεῖλος *lip*, *beak* and *edge*, and no *language*.
The imperfect in short, *was, and kept on being*: the full formula's *one* would stand beside εἷς's headword.

reading: And was, and kept on being, [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[lip|lip, bill and beak, edge and brink and brim and rim]] [[one|one, a single one, one alone]], and [[sound|sound, tone, sound of the voice, cry, faculty of speech and discourse, language, saying]] [[one|one, a single one, one alone]] [[to all|to all, to the whole, to every, to every single]].

greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κινῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν εὗρον πεδίον ἐν γῇ Σεννααρ καὶ κατῴκησαν ἐκεῖ.
hint: Moving from the east, they find a plain in Shinar.

notes.lemma: ἐν τῷ κινῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν
notes.text: The Hebrew *bĕnosʿām miqqedem*, *as they journeyed from the east*. κινέω is *to set in motion, move*; the article and infinitive are one unit with ἐν.
The land of 10:10, glossed again, first in this chapter.

reading: and [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[in the setting in motion|within, inside of, and by means of the setting in motion, the moving, the removing, the meddling with, the applying, the changing and innovating, the rousing and disturbing, the stirring up and arousing and urging on, the setting agoing and causing and calling forth]] of them [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of risings|of risings, of rises, of the quarter of sunrise, of the east]] [[found|found, found out, discovered]] [[a plain|a plain, a flat, a plain flat open country]] [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, the ground]] [[name:Σεννααρ]] and [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and were situate]] [[there|there, in that place]].

names.gloss: (Σεννααρ, from Hebrew Šinʿār, the plain of Babylonia)

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ἄνθρωπος τῷ πλησίον Δεῦτε πλινθεύσωμεν πλίνθους καὶ ὀπτήσωμεν αὐτὰς πυρί. καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῖς ἡ πλίνθος εἰς λίθον, καὶ ἄσφαλτος ἦν αὐτοῖς ὁ πηλός.
hint: Bricks for stone, and asphalt for clay.

notes.text: The Hebrew *wĕhaḥēmār hāyâ lāhem laḥōmer*, *and bitumen was to them for mortar*. ἄσφαλτος is the word of 6:14, where the box was smeared with it; πηλός is *clay*.
Middle Liddell's one sense holds three glosses, *hither! come on! come here!*, the plural of δεῦρο.
πλίνθος, *a brick*, one sense, is plain text.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[man|a man, a human being]] [[to the neighbour|to the neighbour, to the one near and close to and neighbouring, to the one nigh and hard by, to one's neighbour]] [[hither|hither, come on, come here]] [[let us make into bricks|let us make into bricks, let us make bricks, let us build of brick, let us make in the form of a plinth or brick]] bricks and [[let us roast|let us roast, let us broil, let us bake, let us bake and burn, let us bake and harden]] them [[with fire|with fire, with the funeral-fire, with the fire of the hearth]]. and [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]] to them the brick [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[a stone|a stone, a precious stone, marble]], and [[asphalt|asphalt, bitumen]] was to them [[the clay|the clay, the earth, the mud, the mire]].

greek: καὶ εἶπαν Δεῦτε οἰκοδομήσωμεν ἑαυτοῖς πόλιν καὶ πύργον, οὗ ἡ κεφαλὴ ἔσται ἕως τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ποιήσωμεν ἑαυτοῖς ὄνομα πρὸ τοῦ διασπαρῆναι ἐπὶ προσώπου πάσης τῆς γῆς.
hint: A city and a tower whose head reaches heaven, and a name before they are scattered.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *pen-nāpûṣ*, *lest we be scattered*. The Greek has *before being scattered*: the scattering foreseen, not feared.

notes.lemma: οὗ ἡ κεφαλὴ ἔσται ἕως τοῦ οὐρανοῦ
notes.text: The Hebrew *wĕrōʾšô baššāmayim*, *and its top in the heavens*. The Greek has *whose head will be as far as the heaven*: κεφαλή, *head*, the word of 3:15.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἑαυτῶν, the second time; the dative is the Berlin papyrus's, 911.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[hither|hither, come on, come here]] [[let us build a house|let us build a house, let us build, let us build for ourselves]] for ourselves [[a city|a city, a citadel, a country, a body of citizens, a state]] and [[a tower|a tower, the city walls with towers, a movable tower for storming, a tower of defence, the highest part of any building, troops drawn up in close order and a column]], of which [[the head|the head, the whole person, the life, the top, the source, the crown]] will be [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky]], and [[let us make|let us make, let us do, let us produce, let us create]] for ourselves [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[before|before, in front of, further on, sooner, rather than]] [[to be scattered abroad|to be scattered abroad, to be thrown about, to be squandered]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of face|of face, of visage, of countenance, of look, of outward appearance]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ κατέβη κύριος ἰδεῖν τὴν πόλιν καὶ τὸν πύργον, ὃν ᾠκοδόμησαν οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
hint: The Lord comes down to see the city and the tower.

notes.text: The Hebrew *wayyēred YHWH lirʾōt*. καταβαίνω is *to step down*, *to go* or *come down*.
The Hebrew *bĕnê hāʾādām*, *the sons of man*.

reading: and [[stepped down|stepped down, went and came down, went down from, dismounted, came down stairs, went down from the inland parts to the sea, came to land and got safe ashore, went down into the arena, came down from the tribune, came to, ended]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[to see|to see, to perceive, to behold, to look at]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state]] and [[the tower|the tower, the city walls with towers, the movable tower for storming, the tower of defence, the highest part of any building, the troops drawn up in close order and the column]], which [[built a house|built a house, built, built for themselves]] the sons [[of the men|of the men, of the human beings, of mankind]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος Ἰδοὺ γένος ἓν καὶ χεῖλος ἓν πάντων, καὶ τοῦτο ἤρξαντο ποιῆσαι, καὶ νῦν οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἐξ αὐτῶν πάντα, ὅσα ἂν ἐπιθῶνται ποιεῖν.
hint: One race and one lip: nothing they undertake will fail them.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿam ʾeḥād*, *one people*. The Greek has γένος, *race*.

notes.lemma: οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἐξ αὐτῶν πάντα, ὅσα ἂν ἐπιθῶνται ποιεῖν
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lōʾ-yibbāṣēr mēhem kōl ʾăšer yāzmû laʿăśôt*, *nothing that they purpose to do will be withheld from them*. The Greek has *all that they may set themselves to do will not fail from them*: ἐκλείπω, the verb of the water failing at 8:13, and ἐπιτίθημι in the middle.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ποιῆσαι, the aorist; the present is Coislinianus's, M.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: δεῦτε καὶ καταβάντες συγχέωμεν ἐκεῖ αὐτῶν τὴν γλῶσσαν, ἵνα μὴ ἀκούσωσιν ἕκαστος τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ πλησίον.
hint: Come, let us go down and confound their tongue.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *śāpâ*, *lip*, both times: *let us confuse their lip, that they may not hear each one the lip of his neighbour*. The Greek, which said χεῖλος for it at 11:1 and 11:6, has *the tongue* and *the sound* here.
συγχέω, *to pour together, commingle, confound*: the verb of Acts 2:6, where the crowd at Pentecost συνεχύθη, because each heard them speaking in his own language.

reading: [[hither|hither, come on, come here]] and [[having stepped down|having stepped down, having gone and come down, having gone down from, having dismounted, having come down stairs, having gone down from the inland parts to the sea, having come to land and got safe ashore, having gone down into the arena, having come down from the tribune, having come to, having ended]] [[let us pour together|let us pour together, let us commingle, let us confound, let us make ruinous and destroy and obliterate and demolish, let us confound and trouble, let us confound and make of none effect and frustrate]] [[there|there, in that place]] of them [[the tongue|the tongue, the tongue as the organ of speech, the tongue and language, the mouthpiece of a pipe]], [[that|that, in order that]] not [[they may hear|they may hear, they may have hearing of, they may hear tell of, they may know by hearsay, they may hearken and give ear, they may listen to and obey]] [[every|every, every one, each, each one, all and each one, singly and by itself, each by himself]] [[the sound|the sound, the tone, the sound of the voice, the cry, the faculty of speech and discourse, the language, the saying]] [[of the neighbour|of the neighbour, of the one near and close to and neighbouring, of the one nigh and hard by, of one's neighbour]].

greek: καὶ διέσπειρεν αὐτοὺς κύριος ἐκεῖθεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐπαύσαντο οἰκοδομοῦντες τὴν πόλιν καὶ τὸν πύργον.
hint: Scattered over the earth, they stop building the city and the tower.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew, which has *wayyaḥdĕlû libnōt hāʿîr*, *and they left off building the city*. The Greek adds *and the tower*.
παύω is *to make to cease* in the active; the middle, the form here, is *to take one's rest, cease, leave off*. The actives are left out.

reading: and [[scattered abroad|scattered abroad, threw about, squandered]] them [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[from that place|from that place, thence, thereafter, next]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], and [[took their rest|took their rest, rested and ceased and had done, left off from and rested and ceased from, were at rest, left off doing]] [[building a house|building a house, building, building for themselves]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state]] and [[the tower|the tower, the city walls with towers, the movable tower for storming, the tower of defence, the highest part of any building, the troops drawn up in close order and the column]].

greek: διὰ τοῦτο ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Σύγχυσις, ὅτι ἐκεῖ συνέχεεν κύριος τὰ χείλη πάσης τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐκεῖθεν διέσπειρεν αὐτοὺς κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *Bābel*, which the verse ties to *bālal*, *to confuse*. The Greek translates the name, *Confusion*, from συγχέω, the verb of the same verse: the play kept, and the city's name lost. At 10:10 it was Βαβυλών.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* alone the second time; the Greek adds ὁ θεός.
The plural, *the lips*, where the Hebrew has the singular *śĕpat*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads αὐτοῦ, masculine; αὐτῆς, feminine, the city's, is Coislinianus's, M.

greek: Καὶ αὗται αἱ γενέσεις Σημ· Σημ υἱὸς ἑκατὸν ἐτῶν, ὅτε ἐγέννησεν τὸν Αρφαξαδ, δευτέρου ἔτους μετὰ τὸν κατακλυσμόν.

notes.text: The heading of 10:1 again, for Shem's line alone, as far as Abram.
The ordinal, one sense, plain, with no article, as the Greek has none.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone puts ἐτῶν first.

reading: and [[lived|lived, was in full life and strength, was fresh and strong]] [[name:Σερουχ]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[to beget|to beget, to engender, to bring forth, to produce]] him [[name:Ναχωρ]] years two hundred and [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] sons and daughters and [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]].

greek: Καὶ ἔζησεν Ναχωρ ἔτη ἑβδομήκοντα ἐννέα καὶ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Θαρα.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has 29.

reading: And [[lived|lived, was in full life and strength, was fresh and strong]] [[name:Ναχωρ]] years seventy nine and [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Θαρα]].

names.gloss: (Θαρα, from Hebrew Teraḥ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἔζησεν Ναχωρ μετὰ τὸ γεννῆσαι αὐτὸν τὸν Θαρα ἔτη ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι ἐννέα καὶ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας καὶ ἀπέθανεν.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has 119.

reading: and [[lived|lived, was in full life and strength, was fresh and strong]] [[name:Ναχωρ]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[to beget|to beget, to engender, to bring forth, to produce]] him [[name:Θαρα]] years a hundred twenty nine and [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] sons and daughters and [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]].

greek: Καὶ ἔζησεν Θαρα ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτη καὶ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Αβραμ καὶ τὸν Ναχωρ καὶ τὸν Αρραν.
hint: Terah begets Abram, Nahor and Haran.

notes.text: 70, as in the Hebrew.
Abram's brother has the name of his grandfather at 11:22–25, Hebrew *Nāḥôr*, in both texts.

reading: And [[lived|lived, was in full life and strength, was fresh and strong]] [[name:Θαρα]] seventy years and [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Αβραμ]] and [[name:Ναχωρ]] and [[name:Αρραν]].

names.gloss: (Αβραμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrām, "the father is exalted")
(Αρραν, from Hebrew Hārān, of uncertain meaning)

greek: Αὗται δὲ αἱ γενέσεις Θαρα· Θαρα ἐγέννησεν τὸν Αβραμ καὶ τὸν Ναχωρ καὶ τὸν Αρραν, καὶ Αρραν ἐγέννησεν τὸν Λωτ.
hint: The origins of Terah; Haran begets Lot.

notes.text: The heading of 6:9, 10:1 and 11:10, for the Hebrew *tôlĕdōt*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds δέ after the second Θαρα; the Berlin papyrus, 911, does not.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the origins|the origins, the sources, the productive causes, the beginnings, the manners of birth, the races and descents, the productions and generations, the creations and the created things]] of [[name:Θαρα]]; [[name:Θαρα]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Αβραμ]] and [[name:Ναχωρ]] and [[name:Αρραν]], and [[name:Αρραν]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Λωτ]].

names.gloss: (Λωτ, from Hebrew Lôṭ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἀπέθανεν Αρραν ἐνώπιον Θαρα τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ γῇ, ᾗ ἐγενήθη, ἐν τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Χαλδαίων.
hint: Haran dies before his father, in the land of the Chaldeans.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾûr kaśdîm*, *in Ur of the Chaldeans*. The Greek has *in the land of the Chaldeans*, and so does Stephen at Acts 7:4, ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων.
Filed inside ἐνώπιος, whose one tagged translation is *face to face*; the preposition, *like Lat. coram*, is given no English. One translation, so plain text.
The Hebrew *môladtô*, *his birth*: *in which he came into being*.

reading: and [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]] [[name:Αρραν]] face to face of [[name:Θαρα]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather]] of him [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], in which [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]], [[in the space in which a thing is|within, inside of, and by means of the space in which a thing is, the place, the position and post, the place in life and station, the land and country, the piece of land and estate and farm, the country]] of [[name:Χαλδαίων]].

names.gloss: (Χαλδαῖος, the Greek name of Hebrew Kaśdîm)

greek: καὶ ἔλαβον Αβραμ καὶ Ναχωρ ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας· ὄνομα τῇ γυναικὶ Αβραμ Σαρα, καὶ ὄνομα τῇ γυναικὶ Ναχωρ Μελχα θυγάτηρ Αρραν, πατὴρ Μελχα καὶ πατὴρ Ιεσχα.
hint: Abram takes Sarai, and Nahor takes Milcah.

notes.text: Hebrew *Śāray*, Sarai; the Greek Σάρρα, Sarah, of 17:15 and the New Testament, is a different spelling for the changed name.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads καί before the first πατήρ; the Berlin papyrus, 911, alone does not.

reading: and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized]] [[name:Αβραμ]] and [[name:Ναχωρ]] for themselves [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women]]; [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[to the woman|to the woman, to the mistress and lady, to the wife and spouse, to the mortal woman]] of [[name:Αβραμ]] [[name:Σαρα]], and [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[to the woman|to the woman, to the mistress and lady, to the wife and spouse, to the mortal woman]] of [[name:Ναχωρ]] [[name:Μελχα]] daughter of [[name:Αρραν]], [[father|father, grandfather]] of [[name:Μελχα]] and [[father|father, grandfather]] of [[name:Ιεσχα]].

names.gloss: (Σαρα, from Hebrew Śāray, usually connected with śārâ, "princess")
(Μελχα, from Hebrew Milkâ, usually connected with malkâ, "queen")
(Ιεσχα, from Hebrew Yiskâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἦν Σαρα στεῖρα καὶ οὐκ ἐτεκνοποίει.

notes.text: Middle Liddell files it under itself: *a cow that has not calved*, and *of a woman, barren*, citing the New Testament. The first translation heads; the sense the verse uses follows.
τεκνοποιέω in the active is *to bear children*, of the woman, and that is its one active sense, so plain text. The Hebrew is *ʾên lāh wālād*, *she had no child*.

reading: and was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[name:Σαρα]] [[a cow that has not calved|a cow that has not calved, barren]] and not was bearing children.

greek: καὶ ἔλαβεν Θαρα τὸν Αβραμ υἱὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν Λωτ υἱὸν Αρραν υἱὸν τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν Σαραν τὴν νύμφην αὐτοῦ γυναῖκα Αβραμ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῆς χώρας τῶν Χαλδαίων πορευθῆναι εἰς τὴν γῆν Χανααν καὶ ἦλθεν ἕως Χαρραν καὶ κατῴκησεν ἐκεῖ.
hint: Terah takes his family out of the land of the Chaldeans, toward Canaan, as far as Haran.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *mēʾûr kaśdîm*, *from Ur of the Chaldeans*, as at 11:28.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyēṣĕʾû ʾittām*, *and they went out with them*. The Greek has Terah *lead them out*.
νύμφη is *a young wife, bride* first; *daughter-in-law*, the verse's sense, is the entry's fourth, which Perseus leaves untagged.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads τόν before the first υἱόν, and alone leaves out the second Αβραμ.

names.gloss: (Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)
(Χαρραν, from Hebrew Ḥārān, the city Harran)

greek: καὶ ἐγένοντο αἱ ἡμέραι Θαρα ἐν Χαρραν διακόσια πέντε ἔτη, καὶ ἀπέθανεν Θαρα ἐν Χαρραν.

notes.text: 205, as in the Hebrew.
The city is Stephen's Χαρράν at Acts 7:2 and 7:4, Hebrew *Ḥārān*; Abram's brother is *Hārān*, Αρραν.

reading: and [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence]] [[the days|the days, the day-breaks, the times]] of [[name:Θαρα]] in [[name:Χαρραν]] two hundred five years, and [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]] [[name:Θαρα]] in [[name:Χαρραν]].
